summary.text: David Valadao is the Republican incumbent for California's 22nd District, a Hanford dairy farmer and the son of Portuguese immigrants. He served in the California Assembly before his first election to Congress in 2012, lost in 2018 and won the seat back in 2020. His campaign website says he will focus on water, costs, jobs and job training.

paragraphs.text: Valadao was born on April 14, 1977, and raised in Hanford, California. His family emigrated from the Azores Islands of Portugal in 1969 and started a dairy farm in 1973. According to his House biography, the family business now includes two dairies and more than 1,000 acres of farmland in Kings County.

He graduated from Hanford High School in 1995 and attended College of the Sequoias in Visalia. He worked on the family dairy and served as Regional Leadership Council Chairman for Land O'Lakes Inc., and his House biography says he has held leadership roles in dairy organizations and cooperatives.

Valadao was elected to the California State Assembly (30th District) in 2010 and served from 2010 to 2012, including as vice-chair of the Agriculture Committee. In 2012 he was elected to the U.S. House to represent California's 21st District and served from 2013 to 2019.
He lost the 2018 election to TJ Cox and returned to the House after winning the 2020 election. He now represents the 22nd District after redistricting.

In the 2025-2026 Congress Valadao sits on the House Appropriations Committee, where he chairs the Legislative Branch Subcommittee and also serves on the Defense and Agriculture subcommittees. His House biography says he has served on Appropriations throughout his time in Congress and has focused on agriculture and water policy affecting the Central Valley.

His campaign website says he will ‘protect our water, put an end to out-of-control inflation and outrageous gas prices, work to bring new jobs and job training to the Central Valley.’ Valadao and his wife, Terra, whom he married in 1999, have three children, the biography says.
